Hey, our names are Kennedi-Grace and Noah and we are two college students who want to bridge the gap between ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi and its people.
I am Kanaka Maoli and born and raised in Lanaʻi/Hawaiʻi. I am in charge of everything ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (but Noah's learning)!
I am working on the website's development and the technical side, while Kennedi is there to find every issue!

Hey! Our names are Kennedi-Grace Magaoay and Noah Kalma, and we are sophomores at Middlebury College. Kennedi, studying linguistic anthropology, and I, studying computer science and mathematics, are working together to create this website. Beginning toward the end of freshman year, and starting as a little side project, this website came about because Kennedi was telling me about how hard her language, ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian), was to learn online. Me, looking for a project, jumped on the idea. Over time, we both grew more and more invested, and are now working on a full release with lessons, an extensive word bank, and plenty of reference materials and practice!

The Spaced switch gives you a smart schedule. Each word comes back just before you would forget it, so you spend time where it helps most. Flip it on or off any time.
Your deck is the words that are due, plus a few new ones (5 in a small set, 10 in a bigger one). Words that are not due yet stay hidden until their time.
Correct pushes a word further away. Incorrect brings it back soon. In Writing, a right answer on the first try counts as correct; hints and give-ups bring it back sooner.
New and missed words start with short steps: 10 minutes, then 60 minutes. After that the gaps grow: 1 day, 6 days, and longer each time you get it right.
A badge above the card says what is happening. "Review missed" and "Study full set anyway" are practice only: they never change your schedule.

Schedules are kept per word and per mode, so Flashcards and Writing are separate. They save to your account when you are signed in, or to this browser if not.
